name: Ajwa Projects
summary: Ajwa Projects, a Surat-based company incorporated in 2011, provides fabrication, erection, piping, pressure equipment, civil construction and maintenance services to oil and gas, power, steel and cement clients, with over 93% of FY26 revenue coming from Gujarat. Revenue from operations grew from ₹34.3 cr in FY24 to ₹48.4 cr in FY26, and profit rose 65% in FY26 to ₹5.4 cr, an 11.2% net margin with RoNW of 36%. The ₹38 cr issue is ₹30.45 cr fresh and ₹7.6 cr offer for sale by two promoters whose average cost is ₹3.40–₹4.10 a share; the top 10 customers made up about 87% of FY26 revenue. On full-year FY26 profit the post-issue P/E is about 20.6x, well above the two listed peers named in the prospectus (9.5x and 16.0x).

fh1.finding: Revenue from operations rose from ₹34.27 cr (FY24) to ₹48.42 cr (FY26), a CAGR of about 18.9%.

fh2.finding: Revenue grew every year: ₹34.27 cr, ₹36.73 cr, ₹48.42 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh3.finding: Debt to equity was 0.71 in FY26 (borrowings ₹12.52 cr vs net worth ₹17.71 cr) and 0.72 at June 2026.

fh4.finding: Borrowings rose about 15% (₹10.85 cr to ₹12.52 cr) while total income rose about 41% over FY24–FY26.

fh5.finding: Net worth rose every year: ₹8.90 cr, ₹12.29 cr, ₹17.71 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh6.finding: Operating cash flow figures were not found in public sources.

pr1.finding: Profit after tax grew about 65% in FY26, to ₹5.42 cr from ₹3.28 cr.

pr2.finding: Net margin improved from about 8.6% (FY24) to 8.9% (FY25) and 11.2% (FY26).

pr3.finding: Return on net worth was 36.15% in FY26.

pr5.finding: Peer margins were not found in public sources.

va1.finding: Post-issue P/E of about 20.6x on FY26 profit (₹111.65 cr market cap vs ₹5.42 cr PAT) vs a peer median of 12.7x (Atmastco 16.0x, Samay Project Services 9.5x).

va2.finding: Post-issue price to book of about 2.3x (₹111.65 cr market cap vs ₹48.2 cr post-issue net worth) vs a peer median of 1.86x, about 25% higher.

va3.finding: Peer market cap to sales figures were not found in public sources.

va4.finding: No details of priced share issues or transfers in the 12 months before the IPO were found in public sources.

pg1.finding: Promoters hold 65.12% after the issue, down from 98.9%.

pg2.finding: No information on pledged promoter shares was found.

pg3.finding: Related-party transaction figures were not found in public sources.

pg4.finding: Two tax proceedings involving ₹101.32 lakh are outstanding against the promoters.

is1.finding: The offer for sale is ₹7.60 cr, or about 20% of the ₹38.05 cr issue.

is2.finding: The issue is about 34.1% of the ₹111.65 cr post-issue market cap.

is3.finding: The selling promoters' average cost is ₹3.40 and ₹4.10 a share, so ₹203 is about 50–60x their cost.

up1.finding: ₹8.10 cr, or 26.6% of the fresh issue, goes to capex on plant, machinery and transport vehicles.

up2.finding: ₹9.35 cr, or 30.7% of the fresh issue, goes to repaying borrowings.

up3.finding: General corporate purposes take ₹4.43 cr, or 14.55% of the fresh issue.

up4.finding: Public sources don't say whose loans are being repaid.

lg1.finding: One tax proceeding of ₹4.90 lakh is outstanding against the company, under 1% of its ₹17.71 cr net worth.

lg2.finding: No criminal or regulatory cases are listed against the company, promoters or directors.

lg3.finding: Contingent liabilities were not found in public sources.

rk1.finding: The top 10 customers made up about 86.7% of FY26 revenue, and the top customer 26.5% in the June 2026 quarter.

rk2.finding: The top supplier was 10.1% of materials consumed in FY26 (30.9% in FY25, 23.9% in the June 2026 quarter).

rk3.finding: Incorporated in 2011, so about 15 years of operating history.

rk4.finding: Auditor remarks were not found in public sources.
